summary: Intermittent 5xx spike from delayed HTTP/2 ACKs causing streaming sessions to half-close and upstream restarts
description: Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-13 09:10 UTC GreenLeaf AI observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses on streaming routes. Error pattern shows many short-lived streaming sessions ending with upstream connection resets or 502/503 responses. Impact: customer is seeing ~18% failed requests on high-concurrency streaming workloads (conversational chat) leading to degraded UX and increased retry traffic. Environment: prod us-east tenant on Dedicated pool (pool-id d-12).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send concurrent streaming chat requests (50 concurrent streams) against /v1/stream with model=gptx-13b using their websocket-based SDK
2) Maintain each stream with small intermittent client-side pings (keepalive every 10s) for ~30s
3) Observe occasional immediate 502 response from API gateway, or stream resets with HTTP/2 RST_STREAM codes
4) Reproduce more reliably during tenant burst (~>80% of provisioned concurrency)
logs: [apigw-2026-03-13T09:12:21Z] route=/v1/stream tenant=d-12 upstream=10.2.5.83:8443 status=502 msg=upstream_reset reason=half_closed_ack_delay
HTTP/2: received GOAWAY last_stream_id=257 error_code=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM debug='late-ack:200ms'
comments: 2026-03-13 09:25 - Support (Asha Patel): Initial triage complete. Pattern looks like streaming sessions that never fully complete handshake ACKs from upstream before the gateway tears them down. Adding SRE and runtime on-call.

2026-03-13 09:42 - SRE (Diego Morales): Observed correlation between long tail of http2 window updates/ACKs and apigw queuing. CPU on runtime pods increased shortly before resets. Posting Grafana links in #support: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/handshake-latency?from=now-1h

2026-03-13 10:10 - Runtime Eng (Lina Chen): Found a small regression in the runtime backpressure path: slow ACKs cause connection to be marked half-closed and prefetch eviction to intensify, which sometimes trips watchdog when combined with a tenant burst. Creating PR to add jitter and extend half-close timeout.

2026-03-13 12:05 - Support (Asha Patel): Customer notified with temporary mitigation steps (lowering concurrency to 60% of commit, enabling client-side longer keepalive intervals). Customer acknowledged and will apply changes to their SDK configuration.
2026-03-14 08:30 - SRE (Diego Morales): Canary rollout of increased half-close timeout to 5s started for affected pool d-12. Monitoring for reduction in 5xx rate.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: delayed client ACKs (or network reorder) extend HTTP/2 half-closed state; apigw prematurely tears down due to an aggressive half-close timer, cascading into runtime prefetch eviction and occasional watchdog restarts.

Evidence: Grafana shows handshake-latency histogram with a 95th at ~220ms during the spike window; apigw logs flag 'half_closed_ack_delay' and runtime logs show prefetch eviction spikes immediately before pid exits.

Triage actions: captured pcap of a failing stream, reproduced locally with synthetic delayed ACK simulator; confirmed that increasing half-close timeout eliminates RST_STREAM pattern in synthetic run.

Risk: If the true root cause is client network instability, increasing timeouts will reduce 5xx but could raise connection humidity and resource utilization under large bursts. Need to balance with autoscaler rules.

Next steps: coordinate runtime PR rollout, adjust apigw half-close threshold and connection-pool settings, ask customer to bump client keepalive to 20s temporarily, monitor 5xx rate and CPU/memory on runtime nodes.
resolution_notes: Mitigation deployed (2026-03-14): apigw half-close timeout raised from 1s to 5s for pool d-12; runtime backpressure jitter enabled via PR #2874. Temporary customer-side mitigation: lower concurrent streams to 60% and increase keepalive interval to 20s.
Observed outcome: 5xx rate dropped from ~18% to ~2.3% within 30 minutes of mitigations on the canary subset. No further watchdog restarts observed in the canary.

Follow-up: schedule a controlled full-pool rollout after 24h monitoring, add an alert for sustained handshake-latency >150ms, and add a customer-facing doc with recommended streaming SDK keepalive and concurrency guidance.
Postmortem owner: Lina Chen (Runtime). Target postmortem publish date: 2026-03-20.
